articles.title: Iran says ‘desperate’ new sanctions will fail, mediator Pakistan sending army chief to Tehran
articles.summary: Iran said Pakistan’s army chief would visit Tehran on Monday as part of efforts to restore peace and security in the region but gave few details.
articles.body: Iran’s foreign minister dismissed the threat of new U.S. sanctions as a sign of desperation on Sunday and said the expected new measures would fail to defeat Tehran. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who is ⁠due to hold a press conference at 2 p.m. ET on Monday, has threatened to impose “the toughest sanctions in history” on Iran. Iran’s economy is already under huge pressure from international sanctions, its infrastructure has been hit repeatedly, and thousands of people have been killed in airstrikes on the Islamic Republic since the U.S. and Israel launched attacks on Feb. 28. But Tehran remains defiant after nearly six months of war and has brought shipping to a virtual standstill in ⁠the Strait of Hormuz, refusing to allow unauthorized oil tankers to transit a waterway ​that ⁠is vital for global oil shipments. The effective blockade of the strait has pushed up global oil prices. Describing what he said were “repetitive scenarios,” Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in a video posted on Telegram: “The fact that they (U.S. leaders) have ⁠moved on from military operations ... to bring up the same old plans shows that they are desperate.” He said Washington must speak ​to Iran ⁠respectfully to find “a solution based on justice and ‌honor.” “We have never been afraid. All of their actions — whether blockades or other military moves they have made — have failed, and this new issue of theirs will fail as well,” he said. U.S. President Donald Trump has warned of economic consequences against any country that ‌provides “any type of lifeline to Iran” and Bessent has urged cooperation with Washington by China, ‌which buys more than 80% of Iran’s shipped oil, according to 2025 data from analytics firm Kpler. China has urged diplomacy. Pakistan’s army chief to visit Tehran Iran said Pakistan’s army chief, Asim Munir, would visit Tehran on Monday as part of efforts to restore peace and security in the region, but gave few details. Pakistan has been mediating in ⁠the conflict and a Pakistani government source said Munir would touch on recent developments including the U.S. threat of new sanctions. Trump said on Friday that Washington was observing “what happens” in the conflict. “They would love to make a deal, but they’re not ready to make the right deal, in my opinion,” Trump said of Iran. U.S. attacks have severely diminished Iran’s economy and devastated its navy and air force, but Tehran maintains enough missile and drone capability to impede oil tanker traffic and attack regional rivals. Iranian Parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said on Saturday that Tehran had received “numerous messages” from neighboring countries about establishing new regional security arrangements and economic cooperation. Ghalibaf did not say which countries he ‌was referring to. He accused the U.S. of endangering the security of its allies in the region for the sake ​of Israel, adding that an independent, “homegrown” regional order would deliver peace and security. Trump has yet to achieve objectives ‌he set at the start of the war such as dismantling ⁠Iran’s nuclear program — the state of which remains uncertain given that U.N. inspectors have been shut out since 2025 — and creating ⁠conditions for Iranians to overthrow their clerical rulers. While Iran remains defiant, President Masoud Pezeshkian has also called for a diplomatic solution. “It would be better to end the war ‌today, when we are powerful and have dignity, ​and the whole world acknowledges our victory and emphasizes that America, ‌contrary to all regulations, attacked our schools, hospitals, and infrastructure and is ​hated in the world,” the ISNA news agency quoted him as saying on Friday.

articles.title: Candidatos ao governo de RO: confira a agenda desta sexta-feira | G1
articles.standfirst: Confira as atividades de Adailton Furia (PSD), Expedido Netto (PT), Hildon Chaves (União), Marcos Rogério (PL), Samuel Costa (PSB) e Pedro Abib (MDB).
articles.summary: Candidatos ao governo de RO, como Hildon Chaves e Marcos Rogério, realizaram atos de campanha com reuniões e entrevistas nesta sexta-feira.
articles.body:
Nesta sexta-feira (28), cinco dos seis candidatos ao Governo de Rondônia nas eleições de 2026 participaram de atos de campanha. Entre as atividades, estiveram reuniões, caminhadas, gravações de propaganda eleitoral e entrevistas.

O candidato Expedito Netto (PT) não apresentou agenda pública para esta sexta-feira (28).

O candidato do PSD gravou programa eleitoral pela manhã. Ele também cumpriu agenda em Vilhena (RO) e participou de uma ação de distribuição de material de campanha no fim da tarde.

O candidato do União Brasil realizou agenda pela manhã, participou de reuniões e conversou com lideranças. À tarde, participou de uma mobilização com eleitores nas ruas da capital. À noite, realizou uma reunião com lideranças.

O candidato do PSB participou de entrevistas em uma rádio de Ji-Paraná , onde tratou de propostas para o esporte e o lazer. Além disso, participou de um podcast no município de Rolim de Moura.

O candidato do PL fez uma caminhada pela manhã em Vale do Anari (RO). Em seguida, realizou visitas ao centro comercial e a uma feira de negócios em Machadinho d'Oeste (RO). À tarde, gravou programa eleitoral em Ji-Paraná.

O candidato do MDB concedeu entrevistas e também realizou gravações de programa eleitoral durante a manhã. À tarde, reuniu-se com trabalhadores de empresas privadas. Para finalizar a agenda de compromissos públicos, conversou com eleitores em uma live nas redes sociais.

articles.title: Fato ou Fake: sabatina de Augusto Cury a 'O Globo', 'Valor' e CBN | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato à Presidência pelo Avante foi entrevistado nesta sexta-feira (28).
articles.summary: Candidato à Presidência pelo Missão foi entrevistado nesta sexta-feira (28).
articles.body:
Augusto Cury com Milton Jung, Malu Gaspar, Maria Cristina Fernandes e Lauro Jardim na sabatina 'O Globo', CBN e 'Valor' — Foto: Ana Branco/Agência O Globo

O candidato à Presidência pelo Avante , Augusto Cury , foi entrevistado nesta sexta-feira (28) por "O Globo", "Valor "e CBN. Conduzida pelos jornalistas Milton Jung, Lauro Jardim, Malu Gaspar e Maria Cristina Fernandes, a entrevista começou às 10h30 e teve 1h30 de duração.

A série de entrevistas com presidenciáveis de 2026 foi aberta por Romeu Zema ( Novo ) na terça-feira (25). Nos dois dias seguintes, estiveram no estúdio Ronaldo Caiado ( PSD ) e Renan Santos (Missão).

O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ( PT ) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro ( PL ) também foram convidados para as sabatinas, mas não confirmaram presença até o momento. Foram chamados os candidatos melhor colocados na pesquisa divulgada pela Quaest na semana passada, o primeiro levantamento contratado pela TV Globo e pelo "Globo" nesta corrida eleitoral

Terça-feira (25) - Romeu Zema (Novo) – leia a checagem

Quarta-feira (26) - Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) – leia a checagem

Quinta-feira (27) - Renan Santos (Missão) – leia a checagem

Sexta-feira (28) - Augusto Cury (Avante)

A equipe do Fato ou Fake checou as principais declarações de Augusto Cury (Missão). Leia:

"Sabe quantos processos o Supremo [Tribunal Federal] julgou no ano passado? Mais de 112 mil processos."

Segundo o balanço oficial do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), a Corte proferiu 116.170 decisões em 2025, número superior aos 112 mil mencionados.

"Também já treinei a Polícia Militar algumas vezes gratuitamente."

Há registros de mais de uma parceria de Augusto Cury com policiais militares. Em maio de 2019, o então comandante-geral da Polícia Militar de São Paulo, coronel Marcelo Vieira Salles, recebeu Cury para estabelecer uma parceria e disponibilizar aos policiais o programa "Você é insubstituível — Uma vacina emocional contra o suicídio". Na ocasião, Cury também palestrou para oficiais da corporação.

A própria PM de São Paulo informou que o programa seria oferecido gratuitamente e de forma on-line a seus integrantes. Criado por Cury em 2018, o projeto utiliza ferramentas de gestão das emoções e é voltado à prevenção do suicídio e de transtornos emocionais.

Há também registro em Minas Gerais. Documento da Polícia Militar mineira apresentado à Assembleia Legislativa informa que a corporação realizou o minicurso "Você é insubstituível", em parceria com Augusto Cury. Em 2021, a Diretoria de Saúde da PMMG promoveu outro um curso, após o comando firmar parceria com a Academia de Gestão da Emoção, criada por Cury, para trabalhar gestão das emoções e prevenção ao suicídio entre militares.

"Cortaríamos despesas. Temos cerca de 50 mil cargos comissionados."

Dados do Ministério da Gestão e da Inovação em Serviços Públicos mostram que o Executivo possui 50.124 cargos em comissão e funções de confiança em 2025.

"O Brasil tem mais advogados do que todos os países do mundo juntos."

Segundo o Conselho Federal da Ordem dos Advogados do Brasil (OAB), há atualmente cerca de 1,5 milhão de advogados regulares e recadastrados no país até 2025.

Nos Estados Unidos, por exemplo, a American Bar Association (ABA), principal associação nacional de advogados do país, contabilizou 1,37 milhão de profissionais ativos e residentes em 2025. Na Itália, a Cassa Forense registrou 233 mil advogados; na Inglaterra e no País de Gales, a Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) contabilizou 178 mil profissionais em atividade; na Alemanha, a Bundesrechtsanwaltskammer (BRAK) registrou 168 mil; na Espanha, o Consejo General de la Abogacía Española (CGAE) contabilizou 154 mil; e, na França, o Conseil National des Barreaux (CNB) apontou 79 mil. Somados, esses seis territórios reúnem cerca de 2,18 milhões de advogados, aproximadamente 680 mil a mais que os 1,5 milhão registrados no Brasil.

"Eu sou o único que está propondo uma reforma no STF [Supremo Tribunal Federal]. Fim da vitaliciedade: oito anos e vai embora, para nunca mais voltar. E os próximos dois ministros não seriam homens, teriam de ser mulheres."

Romeu Zema (Novo) também divulgou plano com proposta de novo mandato para os ministros do STF com, no mínimo, 15 anos.

Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) defendeu, em 6 de abril deste ano, mandatos de dez anos para ministros do STF. Ele também declarou apoio à proposta da ex-senadora Ana Amélia, que também prevê a proibição de recondução ao cargo.

Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) é um dos signatários da PEC 45/2025, que prevê mandatos de dez anos, sem recondução, e restringe a escolha dos ministros a juízes de carreira.

Fora do pleito eleitoral, a proposta de estabelecer mandatos de oito anos, como dito pelo candidato, sem possibilidade de nova nomeação, também não é inédita. Esse era o conteúdo original da PEC 16/2019, apresentada pelo senador Plínio Valério, conforme divulgado pela Agência Senado.

"Nunca houve tantas recuperações judiciais. 82% das famílias estão endividadas."

O Brasil atingiu recorde de recuperações judiciais em 2025. Segundo a Serasa Experian, 2.466 empresas estiveram envolvidas em pedidos de recuperação judicial, o maior número da série histórica, iniciada em 2012. O levantamento contabilizou 977 processos de recuperação judicial no ano.

A afirmação sobre as famílias também está correta. A Pesquisa de Endividamento e Inadimplência do Consumidor (Peic), da CNC, apontou que 82% das famílias brasileiras estavam endividadas em julho de 2026, maior percentual da série histórica.

Estar endividado não significa estar inadimplente. A pesquisa considera compromissos como cartão de crédito, financiamentos, empréstimos e carnês, mesmo quando estão sendo pagos em dia. Em julho, 29,8% das famílias tinham contas em atraso.

"Nós [Brasil] aumentamos em 148% [o índice de] suicídios entre jovens de 10 a 19 anos (...) porque a síndrome comparativa nas redes sociais é cruel."

O Atlas da Violência 2026, elaborado pelo Instituto de Pesquisa Econômica Aplicada (Ipea) e pelo Fórum Brasileiro de Segurança Pública, apresenta dados específicos para a faixa citada. Entre 2014 e 2024, a taxa de suicídios de pessoas de 10 a 19 anos passou de 2,4 para 3,4 mortes por 100 mil habitantes, um aumento de 41,7%.

Em números absolutos, foram 814 mortes em 2014 e 1.002 em 2024, crescimento de 23,1%. A trajetória não foi continuamente ascendente: entre 2023 e 2024, o levantamento registrou queda de 10,5% no número de mortes.

A associação com as redes sociais exige atenção. O próprio Atlas aponta a comparação com padrões irreais e o cyberbullying entre os fatores de vulnerabilidade para o suicídio, ao lado de depressão, ansiedade e violência. Portanto, isso não demonstra que as redes expliquem, sozinhas, um aumento de 148%

Já em estudos internacionais a respeito do suicídio entre jovens, a Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS) menciona 138% de crescimento, mas referente ao aumento das tentativas de suicídio registradas entre menores de 18 anos na Polônia, de 2020 a 2022, quando foram investigados 2.031 casos. Trata-se, portanto, de outro indicador e de uma população específica, não de uma alta mundial de 148% nas mortes entre jovens de 10 a 19 anos no Brasil.

Participaram da checagem: Anna Julia Steckelberg, Camila da Silva, Luiza Palermo e Lucas Guimarães .

articles.title: Eleições GDF 2026: Candidatos propõem melhorias na saúde e transporte | G1
articles.standfirst: Postulantes ao Palácio do Buriti fizeram caminhadas, carreatas e deram entrevistas. Saúde, educação e mobilidade foram os principais temas abordados.
articles.summary: Candidatos nas Eleições GDF 2026 detalham planos para saúde, educação e transporte em agendas pelo Distrito Federal nesta sexta-feira.
articles.body:
Urna eletrônica — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Candidatos ao Governo do Distrito Federal (GDF) dedicaram a sexta-feira (28) para apresentar propostas aos eleitores em regiões administrativas e em entrevistas.

Saúde, educação e infraestrutura estão entre os temas abordados.

Professor Robson (PSTU) visitou o campus da Universidade de Brasília ( UnB ) em Ceilândia , onde defendeu a criação de casas abrigo com cursos profissionalizantes para mulheres vítimas de violência.

Na área da saúde, prometeu acabar com o Iges-DF e contratar profissionais aprovados em concurso.

"Nossa prioridade é a saúde, porque tem gente morrendo na fila de espera. Nós precisamos extinguir o Iges DF, que mostrou toda a sua ineficiência, e fazer a contratação direta pra saúde", afirmou o candidato, que também se posicionou contra a internação involuntária de pessoas em situação de rua.

Leandro Grass (PT) almoçou no restaurante comunitário do Itapoã e conversou com estudantes na UnB, na Asa Norte.

O candidato prometeu investir na infraestrutura das escolas públicas, reconstruir a carreira docente e aumentar as linhas de ônibus para os universitários do período noturno.

"Eu quero que o aluno de escola publica termine o terceiro ano e ele possa três coisas. Primeiro, que possa realizar o projeto de vida dele, o sonho que ele tem. Depois, que tenha uma profissão, que saia do ensino médio já com uma competência", afirmou.

A candidata à reeleição Celina Leão (PP) fez caminhada no comércio de Santa Maria e prometeu completar as equipes das Unidades Básicas de Saúde (UBS), além de construir novas UPAs.

Ela também defendeu a expansão da Linha 2 do Metrô para atender a região e o Gama .

"É um trecho que a gente tem espaço pra fazer sem ter muita escavação no solo. A previsão de orçamento ficaria uns 13 bilhões de reais, mas metrô você não constrói tudo de uma vez. Você abre licitação da linha 2, busca recurso internacional e aí começa a fazer", explicou.

Arruda (PSD) participou de uma sabatina e fez carreata em Taguatinga . Na região, candidato propôs transferir a sede do governo para o Centro Administrativo (Centrad) para economizar com aluguéis.

O candidato também enfatizou propostas em mobilidade, como expandir o metrô, implementar o Veículo Leve sobre Trilhos (VLT) e construir uma nova ponte sobre o Lago Paranoá.

"Taguatinga primeiro precisa de uma revitalização. Da avenida comercial e do centro da cidade. Tá tudo assim muito desleixado. (...) Eu quero também fazer o VLT aqui pela Hélio Prates, pela comercial até o centro de Taguatinga. O transporte sobre trilhos é o único que organiza a vida da cidade", declarou Arruda.

articles.title: Trilha no TO tem paisagens de impressionar e pedra com formato erótico | G1
articles.standfirst: Formação rochosa curiosa que faz referência ao órgão genital masculino fica na região de Miracema do Tocantins, na região central do estado.
articles.summary: Formação rochosa curiosa que faz referência ao órgão genital masculino fica na região de Miracema do Tocantins, na região central do estado.
articles.body:
Monumento natural em Miracema do Tocantins arranca risadas de visitantes — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram de Pedra do Sol - Miracema-TO

A Trilha da Pedra do Sol, localizada em Miracema do Tocantins , tem atraído visitantes não apenas pelos mirantes panorâmicos e pelo visual encantador do Cerrado, mas também por uma escultura natural inusitada. Entre as diversas formações rochosas, uma pedra de formato fálico, cujo nome faz referência, de forma bem-humorada, ao órgão genital masculino em estado de "cabisbaixo", virou ponto turístico e arranca risadas de quem passa pelo local.

O atrativo fica a cerca de 16 km do centro de Miracema do Tocantins e a 60 km da capital, Palmas. O percurso reúne formações rochosas com detalhes em tons amarelados e mirantes com vista para o relevo das serras e os rios da região, além da ponte que interliga as cidades vizinhas.

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

A comerciante Sirlene Veiga, conhecida como Ciça, organiza expedições com o grupo feminino de trilhas Sport Girl e visitou o local recentemente com duas turmas. Ela conta que a reação das visitantes diante do monumento natural peculiar é sempre de surpresa e diversão.

"É uma pedra que tira muitas risadas e piadas. É engraçado o comportamento de cada uma quando vê: algumas se assustam, outras riem, fazem piadas e outras ficam com vergonha. A gente até brinca chamando de 'pedra da imoralidade', porque ela realmente lembra muito a referência que deram a ela", conta Sirlene.

Apesar das brincadeiras, Ciça destaca que o principal atrativo do lugar continua sendo o contato direto com a natureza e os momentos de contemplação.

"A natureza em si é maravilhosa, um cerradão muito bonito, com pedras gigantescas esculpidas e pontos estratégicos para assistir ao nascer do sol, sentar e refletir. Não é uma trilha para se fazer correndo; a todo momento você quer parar para tirar fotos e contemplar a paisagem", afirma.

De acordo com a condutora ambiental Ludimila Dionízio, o trajeto tem cerca de 4 quilômetros de extensão. O tempo para concluir o percurso varia entre duas e quatro horas, justamente pelo ritmo tranquilo e pelas constantes paradas para registros fotográficos.

"A Trilha Pedra do Sol é uma excelente experiência para quem ama apreciar mirantes e formações rochosas peculiares. Além da pedra que faz alusão ao órgão masculino e arranca boas risadas, o circuito conta com a Pedra do Jacaré e a própria Pedra do Sol, que dá nome ao atrativo. O mais impressionante é o equilíbrio dessa rocha curiosa, que mesmo com o formato inusitado segue firme no lugar", explica a condutora.

Grupo Girls Sports visitam locais turísticos pelo TO e marcaram presença no monumento inusitado — Foto: Reprodução/Arquivo pessoal de Sirlene Veiga

Para aproveitar o passeio com conforto e segurança, a condutora turística recomenda:

Horário de início: Iniciar a caminhada por volta das 5h30 da manhã para acompanhar o nascer do sol e evitar o calor mais intenso do dia.

Vestimenta: Camisas de manga longa com proteção UV, calçados fechados e firmes para caminhada em terreno pedregoso.

Segurança: Uso de perneiras de proteção e lanternas no primeiro trecho (ainda no escuro), geralmente fornecidas pelas agências locais.

Alimentação e hidratação: Levar garrafa de água e um lanche reforçado para a parada no Mirante da Mesa.

Segundo a administradora do local, Dayhohane Azevedo, a trilha tem intensidade entre fácil e moderada. O percurso não conta com subidas íngremes nem descidas perigosas, o que torna o passeio acessível para pessoas de diferentes idades, desde que não tenham limitações físicas severas.

Os visitantes também podem incluir na programação um banho em um braço do Rio Tocantins, que forma um lago particular estruturado pelos proprietários ao fim do percurso. O espaço não oferece serviço de refeições no moment

Entrada apenas para a trilha: R$ 50 por pessoa;

Trilha com banho no Rio Tocantins: R$ 90 por pessoa (acesso a lago particular ao fim do trajeto);

Com mirantes únicos, a vista do nascer do sol na Trilha da Pedra do Sol se torna um momento marcante na vida de quem visita — Foto: Reprodução/Arquivo pessoal de Sirlene Veiga

articles.title: Rodeio Internacional de Barretos: americano tem maior nota na 2ª noite | G1
articles.standfirst: Texano alcançou 92 pontos ao montar o touro Xodó do Patrão na noite desta sexta-feira (28). Competição vai até domingo (30) na arena.
articles.summary: O texano Andrew Alvidrez brilhou no Rodeio Internacional de Barretos ao montar o touro Xodó do Patrão, enquanto Assyrio José Dias assumiu a liderança da classificação.
articles.body:
O americano Andrew Alvidrez, do Texas (EUA), conquistou a maior nota da segunda noite do Rodeio Internacional de Barretos . Na abertura da competição, nesta quinta-feira (27), a participação do atleta ficou marcada pelas quatro tentativas frustradas de completar uma montaria. Já nesta sexta-feira (28), o peão deu a volta por cima e mostrou que está na disputa pelo título no Barretão.

A segunda rodada contou com a participação dos 36 competidores. Andrew foi o grande destaque ao alcançar 92 pontos sobre o touro Xodó do Patrão, da Companhia Califórnia. Com o resultado, o americano obteve a maior nota da noite e também da competição até o momento, superando os 91,50 pontos de Cássio Dias.

Andrew Alvidrez conquista maior nota da 2ª noite do Rodeio Internacional de Barretos — Foto: Reprodução/BRTVMAX

Cássio, que brilhou na abertura , não conseguiu repetir o desempenho nesta sexta-feira. O atleta montou o touro Show Time, da Companhia Guto Paglione, mas foi derrubado após um salto alto do animal logo no início da apresentação.

Outros competidores que fizeram boas montarias no primeiro dia também não conseguiram pontuar na segunda rodada. São eles: Lucas Vinicius Almeida, com o touro Praiano, da Companhia Guto Paglione; João Paulo Velasco, com Babado Novo, da Gutt Bulls; e o americano Keyshawn Whitehorse, com Rancor, da Máfia dos Boi.

Touro empina a traseira para tentar derrrubar peão na segunda noite de Rodeio Internacional de Barretos 2026 — Foto: Érico Andrade/g1

Na contramão, o bicampeão do The American, João Ricardo Vieira, e o campeão da etapa de Barretos da PBR Brasil, Gabriel Henrique da Silva, pontuaram pelo segundo dia consecutivo.

De volta ao Rodeio Internacional de Barretos após a última participação, em 2018, João Ricardo conquistou 85,75 pontos ao montar o touro Cara Metade , da Companhia GM/5 Estrelas.

Já Gabriel Henrique da Silva, de Lagoa Formosa (MG), segue invicto na competição e em todas as montarias que disputou até o momento em Barretos. Nesta sexta-feira, ele marcou 89,25 pontos sobre o touro Tizil, da Companhia Leandro Bueno.

Peão tenta se manter 8 segundos em cima do touro em disputa pelo título do Rodeio Internacional de Barretos 2026 — Foto: Érico Andrade/g1

Com os resultados da noite, a classificação sofreu mudanças. Cássio Dias, que havia assumido a liderança na abertura, caiu para a décima colocação. Após a soma das notas das duas rodadas, o novo líder é Assyrio José Dias, com 176,50 pontos. Veja como ficou o ranking:

Gabriel Henrique da Silva: 174,45 pontos

A disputa pelo título do Rodeio Internacional acontece neste domingo (30), último dia da 71ª edição da festa.

articles.title: Veja o que fizeram os candidatos ao governo do AM nesta sexta-feira (28) | G1

articles.summary: O primeiro turno será em 4 de outubro. O segundo está marcado para o dia 25 do mesmo mês.
articles.body:
Candidatos ao governo do Amazonas nas eleições de 2026 realizaram visitaram feiras, maternidade e concederam entrevista à emissora de TV nesta sexta-feira (27), em Manaus .

O primeiro turno será em 4 de outubro. O segundo está marcado para o dia 25 do mesmo mês.

articles.title: Trump anuncia acordo que garante controle de petróleo da Venezuela | G1
articles.standfirst: País sul-americano possui as maiores reservas conhecidas de petróleo do mundo, com 303 bilhões de barris. País está sob influência americana desde que governo Trump sequestrou e depôs Maduro, em janeiro deste ano.
articles.summary: País sul-americano possui as maiores reservas conhecidas de petróleo do mundo.
articles.body:
O presidente dos EUA, Donal Trump, anunciou nesta sexta-feira (28) um acordo que garante aos EUA o controle de reservas de petróleo da Venezuela equivalentes a 65 bilhões de barris, ou cerca de 21% de todo o petróleo do país .

A Venezuela se encontra sob ampla influência americana desde que o governo Trump sequestrou e depôs Nicolás Maduro , em janeiro deste ano (leia mais abaixo) .

"Sob minha orientação, o Secretário de Estado Marco Rubio e o Secretário de Guerra Pete Hegseth — trabalhando em estreita colaboração com a altamente respeitada Presidente interina da Venezuela, Delcy Rodriguez, e por meio de uma parceria com o setor privado — garantiram o controle majoritário dos EUA sobre mais de 65 BILHÕES DE BARRIS de reservas comprovadas de petróleo na Venezuela, sem qualquer custo para o contribuinte americano", escreveu Trump na sua rede social, a Truth Social.

A Venezuela é o país com as maiores reservas conhecidas de petróleo do mundo, estimado em 303 bilhões de barris . Atualmente, o país sul-americano produz cerca de 1,25 milhão de barris de petróleo bruto por dia.

Esse controle ocorrerá, segundo Trump, por meio de parcerias com empresas privadas. Os detalhes do acordo não estão imediatamente claros.

Trump disse que o acordo mais do que dobraria as reservas de petróleo dos Estados Unidos .

Tanques com o logo da PDVSA em refinaria em Curaçao — Foto: Andres Martinez Casares/Reuters

O governo Trump está sob pressão, antes das eleições de meio de mandato previstas para novembro, devido à alta dos preços da gasolina — situação que poderia ser amenizada com o acesso a petróleo mais barato e o aumento da produção. Os EUA também buscam soluções para recompor sua Reserva Estratégica de Petróleo, incluindo a possibilidade de realizar trocas de petróleo bruto com produtores americanos.

Desde que os EUA capturaram e removeram o ex-presidente Nicolás Maduro do poder em janeiro, Washington tem tentado garantir um fluxo estável de petróleo bruto venezuelano para as refinarias americanas.

Trump fala com a imprensa na Casa Branca após assinar ordem executiva renomeando o Lago Ontário como Lago América — Foto: Evan Vucci/Reuters

Em 3 de janeiro, uma operação militar americana realizou uma invasão ao país, sequestrando o presidente Nicolás Maduro.

Maduro foi levado a Nova York, onde se encontra preso aguardando julgamento.

Em seu lugar, foi nomeada como presidente interina Delcy Rodríguez, vice de Maduro, mas cujo governo tem tomado medidas pró-Washington, como a soltura de dissidentes políticos e o envio de petróleo para os EUA .

Marco Rubio durante evento em Washington em 4 de agosto de 2026. — Foto: Kevin Lamarque/Reuters

O secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, é apontado como a autoridade que dita de fato as ordens em Caracas .

O republicano tem defendido uma aproximação com Caracas principalmente por causa da importância do país no mercado de petróleo. O tema ganhou ainda mais relevância para a Casa Branca após a escalada do conflito com o Irã, que pressionou os preços internacionais da commodity.

Ao mesmo tempo, a oposição venezuelana e entidades de defesa dos direitos humanos têm pedido um avanço mais rápido das negociações políticas. A cobrança também encontra apoio entre parlamentares democratas e republicanos no Congresso dos Estados Unidos.

Rubio já havia defendido que a Venezuela passaria por três etapas após a saída de Maduro: estabilização econômica, reorganização política e uma transição para eleições.

articles.title: Renan Santos propõe guerra a facções e metas para gestores em MG | G1
articles.standfirst: Em agenda em MG, candidato à Presidência também apresentou propostas para áreas dominadas por facções, habitação, dívida dos estados e infraestrutura.
articles.summary: Em Minas Gerais, Renan Santos detalhou planos para segurança e a criação de uma lei para punir prefeitos e governadores que não atingirem metas de gestão.
articles.body:
Foto do candidato Renan Santos durante coletiva de imprensa em BH — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

O candidato à Presidência Renan Santos cumpriu agenda em Minas Gerais nesta sexta-feira (28) e apresentou propostas para segurança pública, saneamento básico, habitação, infraestrutura e renegociação das dívidas dos estados.

Na área de segurança, Renan defendeu aumento de penas, mudanças nas leis de execução penal, construção de superpresídios e ações para retomada de territórios dominados por facções criminosas.

Durante a tarde, ele participou de uma ação para apagar símbolos de facções pintados em muros e afirmou que o país precisa promover uma "guerra contra as facções criminosas".

"Aumento de pena para todos, alteração às leis de execução penal e uma política de enfrentamento urbana", afirmou.

O candidato também propôs colocar determinadas regiões, bairros e até cidades em estado de defesa para realizar o que chamou de "reocupação territorial" por meio das polícias, com as Forças Armadas como auxiliares.

"A gente vai retirar o comando territorial que essas facções têm sobre territórios brasileiros", disse.

Renan também defendeu a criação da chamada Lei de Responsabilidade Gerencial, que estabeleceria metas para prefeitos e governadores em áreas como segurança, saúde, educação e saneamento básico.

Segundo o candidato, o cumprimento dos indicadores poderia ser considerado na distribuição de investimentos e emendas. Gestores que não atingissem determinadas metas poderiam sofrer sanções.

"Se eles cumprem esses pontos, eles podem receber mais investimentos, inclusive emendas. Se não cumprem, o prefeito pode ficar inelegível", afirmou.

Na área habitacional, Renan propôs o que chamou de "marco nacional de desfavelização". A medida incluiria um cadastro nacional das habitações e ações urbanísticas em comunidades.

Segundo o candidato, famílias que vivem em locais considerados inadequados para moradia poderiam ser transferidas para novos bairros, construídos mais próximos de áreas com oferta de emprego. Em outras regiões, ele defendeu parcerias com a iniciativa privada para investimentos.

Ao falar sobre as dívidas estaduais, Renan defendeu que novas renegociações sejam condicionadas à realização de reformas previdenciárias e administrativas pelos estados.

"Ou todo mundo começa a fazer as mesmas reformas que nós, do governo federal, vamos fazer, ou o Brasil vai ficar fingindo estar vivendo uma normalidade", afirmou.

O candidato também defendeu uma revisão do pacto federativo e disse que Minas Gerais está entre os estados menos beneficiados pela atual distribuição de recursos da União.

Renan também apresentou propostas para melhorar a infraestrutura viária. Segundo ele, a precariedade de rodovias e a falta de ferrovias adequadas aumentam os custos para o escoamento da produção.

O candidato defendeu ampliar os investimentos públicos em infraestrutura e afirmou que regiões com produção consolidada, mas prejudicadas pela falta de estrutura para transporte, teriam prioridade.

Segundo Renan, parte dos recursos viria de cortes de gastos obrigatórios previstos em uma nova âncora fiscal defendida por ele.

"Tudo o que eu cortar de gastos obrigatórios, eu vou transformar em investimento em infraestrutura", disse.

articles.title: 178 Questions to Ask Someone to Get to Know Them Better
articles.summary: These 178 questions to ask to get to know someone cover everything from relationships and family to values, goals, careers, and everyday habits.
articles.body:
There's a reason "So, tell me about yourself" is such a terrible conversation starter. It's broad, vaguely terrifying, and somehow makes even the most interesting person forget everything they've ever done in their life. Whether you're on a first date , getting to know a new friend, or realizing you've somehow been dating someone for six years without knowing their go-to karaoke song, asking the right questions can make learning about someone a whole lot easier.

And no, that doesn't mean showing up to drinks with a Notes app full of questions and working your way down the list (but do you). The point isn't to interrogate someone; it's to give the conversation somewhere interesting to go. "A unique question can snap someone out of autopilot and make them reflect and want to connect," says Karen Vincent, LCSW, therapist and clinical director at Octave

The real magic, though, is in what happens after you ask. Rather than immediately moving on to your next question, Vincent recommends actually listening to the answer and following whatever seems to light the other person up. "The first question cracks open the door, but the follow-up questions are where you get the real connection," she says. If they tell you their dream vacation is two weeks in Japan, ask why Japan! What would they want to do there? Have they always wanted to go? Congratulations, you're having a conversation .

Of course, not every question is right for every person or every stage of a relationship. Pay attention to how they respond, says Vincent. If they're sharing details and seem excited to keep talking, you can probably dig a little deeper. If they give a short answer, change the subject, or seem uncomfortable, take the hint and move along. With that in mind, consider the questions ahead conversation starters , not a checklist—from general likes and dislikes to relationships, values, daily habits, and future goals, there are plenty of ways to get to know someone better.

Consider these questions great starting points and icebreakers to scratch the surface. They're especially useful for first dates and conversations on dating apps. Vincent recommends starting with casual topics and letting the other person's answers guide where the conversation goes from there. The questions near the top are lighter than the ones near the bottom, so start wherever feels natural and see where the convo takes you.

If you could have dinner with one person (living or dead), who would it be?

If you could have any animal as a pet, what would you choose?

What's something you could talk about for hours?

Oh, no! There's a spider in the house. What's the move?

Have you ever become intensely invested in the fate of a TV show character?

Which TV or movie character do you identify with and why?

Do you like going to the movies or would you rather wait until it's available on streaming services?

If your life were a movie, what scene would you watch over and over again?

Have you ever met any celebs? If so, what were they like?

Are you Team Spotify or Team Apple Music?

What type of music do you like the most?

What's the best concert you've ever been to?

Who would you drain your savings to see live?

What song or artist do you love that people might not expect?

Have you ever read a book that changed your life?

What was the best trip you've ever been on?

Would you prefer to go camping or chill at a resort?

When you vacation, do you prefer a relaxed vibe or something adventurous and/or touristy?

What's your ideal way to spend your birthday?

Where are you most likely to be at a party?

If you were an animal, what animal would you be?

If you could instantly become an expert at one thing, what would it be?

What do most people overestimate or underestimate about you?

What's a moment you'd love to be a fly on the wall for?

What scrambles your brain every time you think about it?

What's your "and then it got worse" story?

What's something you can never have too many of?

When was the last time you felt really excited, and what were you excited about?

What's the funniest thing your inner child wants?

What movie always makes you sad? What movie makes you happy?

Does social media make you feel better or worse about yourself?

What's the best decision you've made in your life?

What's the best decision you've made today?

What are some of your biggest irrational fears?

What makes you feel most appreciated by other people?

What do you love most in your life right now?

What's the last thing you remember wishing for?

What's something you love completely unapologetically?

What's the best gift you've ever received?

What's the worst gift you've ever received?

When was the last time you got really angry, and why?

Complete this sentence: "I most enjoy having someone to do _____ with."

What's one question you wish more people asked you?

Learning about someone's childhood can tell you a lot about the experiences, people, and places that helped shape them. Some of these questions are light, while others get pretty personal, so pay attention to how the other person responds as you go. Vincent notes that someone might happily open up about one area of their life but become noticeably quieter around another, and continuing to push can work against connection. In other words: Read the room, respect their boundaries, and don't assume every childhood story is first-date material.

Where did you grow up? Is it the same place you were born?

Did you collect anything, like cards or coins?

What phase did you go through as a kid or teenager that makes you laugh now?

What was your favorite birthday growing up?

What embarrassing moment has stuck with you over the years?

What was your favorite vacation growing up?

Were you pretty well behaved in school, or were you a troublemaker?

Did you ever go to detention for anything?

Did you play any sports or instruments as a kid? Do you still play them now?

Did you ever go on any really exciting field trips?

What trend or phase were you completely obsessed with growing up?

What has surprised you the most about adulthood?

What would you tell your childhood self?

Who did you turn to as a child when you were going through something tough?

What's something difficult you went through growing up that taught you something about yourself?

What's something about the way you grew up that you appreciate more now than you did at the time?

The people someone chooses to keep close can tell you a lot about what they value in their relationships. And if you're dating, learning about their family and friendships can also help you understand what role those relationships might play in their life going forward. Just remember that family can be a sensitive subject, and "family" can mean something different to everyone, so let the other person decide how much they want to share.

What is your relationship like with your family?

What did spending time together as a family look like growing up?

What traits from the people who raised you do you hope you never pick up?

What traits from the people who raised you do you hope to carry with you?

What five words would you use to describe the person or people who raised you?

Do you have any cousins you're close to?

Did you have a close bond with any of your grandparents?

Who do you call first when something big happens?

Does your family have any traditions you really love?

If you ended up in jail, what would your friends and family think you did?

How did you meet the majority of your friends?

Do you and your friends have any annual traditions?

What's your favorite memory with your friends?

Are you comfortable being friends with your coworkers or would you rather keep those relationships professional?

What quality do you value most in a friend?

Questions About Dating and Relationships

Okay, now we're getting a little more personal. If you're getting to know someone romantically, questions about their dating history and what they're looking for can tell you a lot about whether you're actually on the same page. That doesn't mean you need their complete romantic résumé on date one, though. Start with the lighter stuff and save questions about exes and past breakups for whenever it feels natural.

Tell me about the best date you've ever been on.

Tell me about the worst date you've ever been on.

What's the best way someone could flirt with you?

Would you prefer to meet people online or in person?

Have you been in a serious relationship before?

If you're comfortable sharing, what did you learn from your last relationship?

What do you look for and value most in a long-term partner?

What qualities do you have that make you a good partner?

What kind of relationship are you looking for now?

Are there any couples whose relationship you really admire?

Talking about politics, religion, and personal values can feel a little intimidating when you're getting to know someone, but these topics can also tell you pretty quickly whether you're fundamentally compatible. You don't need to launch into a debate five minutes after meeting, obviously, but once the conversation feels comfortable, asking about the things that matter to someone can help you get to know them on a much deeper level. Just remember that these questions go both ways: If you're going to ask someone to share their beliefs, be prepared to share yours too.

Were you raised with any particular religious or spiritual beliefs?

Do you currently have any religious or spiritual beliefs?

Are there any social issues that you really care about? Why do they matter to you?

Do you feel strongly about any specific charitable causes?

Have you ever volunteered for an organization?

Talking about work can tell you a lot about someone's day-to-day life, what motivates them, and how important their career is to them. The key is keeping it conversational rather than making them feel like they accidentally wandered into a job interview. You're trying to learn what their life looks like, not where they see themselves in five years. (Unless you're genuinely curious, in which case, go off.)

How did you decide what to do for a living?

Would you say you feel fulfilled at work?

What's the most fulfilling part of your job?

What's the most stressful part of your job?

Do you want to stay in your current role for a while?

What's your favorite part of the workday?

If money wasn't a factor, would you still choose the career you did?

What would make you feel like you've "made it" in your career?

Have you ever dealt with imposter syndrome?

Do you see yourself doing this kind of work long-term, or is there something else you'd eventually like to do?

If you could start a business, what would it be?

Questions about goals—especially big dreams—can tell you a lot about what someone is working toward and what motivates them. And while career goals are part of that, these questions are more about the bigger picture: where they want to live, what they want to experience, and what they hope their life eventually looks like. Some get more personal than others, so, as always, you don't need to ask about marriage and kids before you've finished your first drink.

What's the next big purchase you want to make?

What would you do if you won the lottery?

What are you most determined to accomplish?

Is there an area of your life where you feel like something is missing?

What's something you hope is different about your life five years from now?

If money wasn't a factor, what would your dream life look like?

Do you see yourself getting married someday?

Do you see yourself having kids someday?

Would you ever want to live abroad for a while?

Questions About Their Daily Routine and Habits

Okay, asking someone what time they wake up might not lead to the most thrilling conversation of your life, but learning about their everyday habits can tell you a surprising amount about what being part of their life might actually look like. Are they up at 5 a.m. while you consider anything before 9 an emergency? Do they spend every weekend out with friends while your ideal Saturday involves never leaving the couch? You certainly don't need identical routines to be compatible, but it can be helpful to know how someone actually spends their time.

Are you a morning person or a night owl?

What's the best way to wake up in the morning?

What does your morning routine look like?

How do you take your coffee? Or are you more of a tea person?

What's the first thing you do when you finish work?

Do you have a favorite neighborhood spot you go to all the time?

What's your go-to meal when you don't feel like cooking?

What meal is your favorite: breakfast, lunch, or dinner?

Do you have a favorite restaurant in your neighborhood?

Are you a neat person or a messy person?

articles.title: Yemen’s divided education system leaves students’ futures in limbo
articles.summary: Students in Houthi areas fear lost opportunities after government decision not to authenticate some certificates.
articles.body:
Sanaa, Yemen – Bashar Mohammed has enrolled in multiple English-language courses since he finished high school last year.

The 19-year-old is intent on improving his language skills, hoping to land a scholarship to pursue undergraduate studies abroad.

With a good command of English and a high school certificate, Mohammed believes he can one day secure an opportunity to study at a university overseas.

But because he completed high school in the Yemeni capital Sanaa, which is under the control of the Houthi rebel group , Mohammed now worries that government authorities in Aden will not validate his academic credentials.

Yemen has been divided between the internationally-recognised government and the Houthis since the country’s war started more than a decade ago.

The Aden-based government Education Ministry issued a circular in late July suspending the authentication of some school certificates issued in Houthi-controlled areas. The ministry said in early August that it could not access official records needed to verify some students’ documents, blaming the Houthis for the problem.

Students have been left in the middle of the quagmire, uncertain of how it will be resolved.

“It amounts to saying that our 12 years of schooling were a waste of time. This is painful,” Mohammed told Al Jazeera.

It also means that, for now, the dream of studying abroad is over. Yemenis who want to leave the country to study must have their certificates authenticated by the government’s Foreign Ministry, but that won’t happen without a stamp from the Education Ministry confirming that the certificate is genuine.

Ayman Ahmed, an 18-year-old who just graduated from high school in Houthi-controlled Raymah province, said it was students who were being punished, not the Houthis.

“The students and their parents are powerless, and they cannot go against the Houthis or ask Houthi authorities to coordinate with the government in Aden,” Ahmed said, highlighting the dangers of dissent against the rebel group, who have imprisoned many opponents and UN staff . “So, treating our certificates as invalid is collective punishment, and it is unfair.”

Earlier this month, the government’s Minister of Education Adel al-Abadi clarified that the suspension of certificate authentications in Houthi-controlled areas does not apply to all academic years. He said that the ministry has access to student records for some years, allowing it to verify and authenticate certificates issued during those periods.

“There are certificates for which there is no data in the ministry’s records, and therefore it is difficult for us to verify their validity and accuracy,” Al-Abadi said.

But Ahmed said that wasn’t the fault of the students now affected.

“The education officials in Sanaa and Aden can coordinate and resolve the issue of the missing data,” he said. “Our education and certificates should not be a victim of their disputes.”

With Yemen’s geography fragmented between the Houthis and the Yemeni government since 2015, each side has adopted its own education policies, creating two parallel systems.

The school year, for example, begins in June in areas controlled by the Houthis, while schools in areas under the control of the government reopen at the end of August. The school curricula have also diverged, with the Houthis making numerous alterations to the previous textbooks.

“There are two systems, two ministries, with zero coordination,” said Mohammed Abdu, a sociology researcher at Taiz University. “Society, and in particular the students, cannot escape the negative impact of this imbalance.”

Abdu explained that in addition to the different calendars and curricula, Yemen’s two competing education systems have different high school test formats, as well as different dates for those exams.

The recent uptick in fighting in Yemen , which has threatened to drag the country back into all-out war after a relatively quiet four years, is likely to cause further problems for students, Abdu said. He pointed out that violence would likely displace families and damage schools, like previous rounds of the war.

According to the United Nations, around 2,800 schools in Yemen have been destroyed or damaged, or used for purposes other than education because of the war.

And, the UN says, more than 6.6 million children were out of school in Yemen this year – about one-third of the country’s school-age children.

“The warring sides had better reach a consensus on a policy that mitigates the ordeal of Yemeni students and distances education from political or military rivalries,” Abdu said.

Aref Naji Ali, an advisor with the Ministry of Education in Aden, told Al Jazeera that the continued division in educational policies is one of “the most dangerous consequences of the Yemeni conflict”.

“Education should not become another arena for political division. Students are the most vulnerable, and it is unjust for them to bear the brunt of the division between institutions and authorities,” Ali said.

While Ali defended the Aden-based Education Ministry’s decision to suspend the endorsement of certificates that it was unable to verify, he put the blame on the Houthis.

“Our responsibility is to protect the right to education and preserve the legality of the educational process and the national educational identity so that the current division doesn’t become a permanent rift in the minds of future generations,” Ali said.

But for those impacted, that sentiment isn’t enough.

Ammar Amri, a schoolteacher in Sanaa, is angry that his students are being robbed of the opportunities he believes they deserve.

“Many of the students have the academic ability and financial means to pursue education abroad,” Amri said. “With this ongoing conflict, many dreams will be shattered.”

“This is a loss for the students and a loss for society as a whole,” he added. “It appears that the warring sides have cut education from their list of priorities, and it does not concern them.”

articles.title: Canada poaches dozens of US academics as Trump administration tightens university funding
articles.summary: Forty-eight academics come from institutions in the US, including Harvard, Cornell, and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, and from a range if disciplines.
articles.body: Canada has recruited dozens of academics from American campuses as the United States cracks down on prestigious institutions. On Thursday, Canadian Industry Minister Mélanie Joly announced the hiring of 64 scholars, who will be supported by more than 500 million Canadian dollars (more than $350 million) for eight years at several universities in Canada. Forty-eight of the academics will come from institutions in the US, including Harvard, Cornell, and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. They come from a range of disciplines, including medicine, engineering, and climate science. US President Donald Trump’s administration has targeted a set of elite colleges and universities since he returned to office, exerting control by cutting them off from federal funding. Researchers have also expressed concern over the White House’s increasing power over who receives scientific grants. The concerns have led to turmoil as academics at colleges and universities in the US consider the future of their research. “While certain countries are cutting research and turning their back on academic freedom, we’re doubling down on science and we’re doubling down on research,” Joly said at a press conference at the University of British Columbia (UBC) on Thursday. When asked whether she believes Trump will view the hirings as an escalation of the trade war, Joly said that the move represents Canada making its own decisions. “The US administration is taking its own decisions and we’re taking ours,” Joly said. ”We’re very glad that these fantastic professors are coming.” CNN has reached out to the White House for comment. The funding for the researchers comes from Canada’s Global Impact+ Research Talent Initiative, a 1.7 billion Canadian dollars (more than $1.2 billion) effort to “attract world-leading researchers to Canada.” The institutions that hired the professors celebrated the move in a series of statements. Dr. Benoit-Antoine Bacon, the president and vice-chancellor of UBC, which hired nine of the researchers, said that the university is “delighted to welcome these nine exceptional researchers, whose work will have important and meaningful impact.” “This vital government support is helping Canada build an extraordinary foundation of research excellence amid an uncertain international landscape, said Melanie Woodin, president of the University of Toronto, where six researchers will work. Some of the researchers cited concerns over academic freedom in the US as contributing to their decision. Phillip Zamore, a researcher of RNA biology at the University of Massachusetts, told NPR affiliate WBUR that he decided to depart his institution after recruitment became an issue. “I cannot do my best work in America,” said Zamore. “I can’t recruit the best people to help me do that, and I can’t promise them an environment where they’ll be safe.” Ethan Zuckerman, a media scholar who will leave the University of Massachusetts Amherst for McGill University, said in a statement that he saw it as an opportunity to join a team doing “groundbreaking work.” “Canada’s willingness to support research that challenges commercial and political threats to democracy is deeply necessary at a moment where authoritarianism is on the rise around the globe,” he said.

articles.title: US plans to cut off military aid to key Middle East ally, BBC told
articles.summary: Iraqi Kurdistan fears the Trump administration's plan will make the region more vulnerable to further attacks from Iran.
articles.body:
The Trump administration is planning to cut off military aid to a key Middle East ally that helped the US defeat the Islamic State group (IS) and is now facing punishing attacks from Iran, according to four sources familiar with the matter.

The US Department of Defense has told leaders of Iraq's semi-autonomous Kurdistan region in recent meetings that the administration is not planning to renew an expiring agreement that provides security assistance to the Peshmerga, the Kurdish security force.

The BBC spoke to two officials who participated in the talks and two other sources with direct knowledge of the issue. The sources spoke on the condition of anonymity to describe the talks, details of which have not been previously reported.

Kurdish officials fear the funding cut would create a power vacuum and embolden Iran, which has fired hundreds of missiles and drones into Iraqi Kurdistan since US President Donald Trump started the war with Tehran.

Ending the Peshmerga's security assistance would undermine a longtime partner in Iraq, analysts said, and send the message that the US cannot be trusted to back its allies in the region.

"The US would be cutting off the Kurds, who shed so much blood to help the Americans achieve their goals in Iraq and the wider Middle East," Yerevan Saeed, the director of the Global Kurdish Initiative for Peace at American University, said.

"This is going to be a big win for Iran, China, and Russia if the Kurds are left so exposed."

In his second term, Trump has pledged to reduce America's foreign entanglements in regions like the Middle East. He also launched the war with Iran, which reached the six-month mark on Friday with no end in sight.

The memorandum of understanding between the Pentagon and the Kurdish Regional Government (KRG) is set to expire on 30 September, the same day the US and other nations are withdrawing their last remaining troops from Iraq.

The troop withdrawal will formally end the international military campaign against IS, in which the Peshmerga fought alongside coalition troops to end the jihadist group's control of parts of Iraq and Syria. The sole remaining US military base in the country, located in the Iraqi Kurdish capital of Irbil, is set to close next month once coalition troops leave.

The Peshmerga, which has approximately 180,000 troops in Iraqi Kurdistan, received $61m (£45m) in the fiscal year 2026 for weapons, military training and stipends through the Pentagon's counter-IS programme.

The Pentagon proposed cutting all the group's security aid in its fiscal year 2027 budget request - arguing that since IS was defeated the money should now be reallocated - but the spending plan is on hold amid a broader budget battle in Congress.

The request raised alarm bells in Iraqi Kurdistan, but officials had held out hope that the US would renew the funding through an extension of the current deal.

The fears have only grown as Iran has stepped up attacks against the KRG. Iran and Iranian-backed militias had conducted 158 missile or drone attacks inside Iraqi Kurdistan by late May, according to reasearch on the latest available data compiled by the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, a Washington DC think tank.

But despite the surge in attacks, in recent talks with Iraqi and Kurdish leaders, defence department officials said the US was not planning to extend the memorandum of understanding, multiple sources with knowledge of the discussions said. The Pentagon signed the initial memorandum of understanding giving military assistance to the Peshmerga in 2016 and renewed it in 2022.

A final decision on security engagement between the US and Kurdistan is still being reviewed, according to one source familiar with the Pentagon's thinking. The US is considering ways to maintain some security support in both Iraq and Iraqi Kurdistan after the troop withdrawal, the sources said.

Six months into the Iran war, what has Trump accomplished?

The KRG declined to comment. The White House referred the BBC to the Pentagon where a spokesperson pointed to a statement by the department summarising Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's meeting with Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi in July.

"The United States, Iraq and Coalition partners have achieved tremendous success in defeating ISIS and now the Iraqi Security Forces, including the Peshmerga and other Iraqi Kurdistan Region security forces, will lead the fight against terrorists in Iraq," the statement said.

A State Department spokesperson told the BBC it was focused on implementing the troop withdrawal, and "ensuring that Prime Minister Zaidi is positioned to disarm Iran-aligned terrorist militias and safeguard Iraqi sovereignty."

The expiration of the security aid for the Peshmerga would come less than one year after the US opened its largest consulate in the world, in Irbil.

At the ribbon-cutting ceremony for the $800m complex last December, Michael Rigas, a senior US State Department official, said the consulate was "a testament to the value of the relationship between the United States and the Iraqi Kurdistan Region".

The recent discussions around Kurdish security were part of larger conversations between the US, the Iraqi government and KRG over the upcoming troop withdrawal. That date was set under a 2024 agreement between Washington and Baghdad to withdraw the US troops that remain in Iraq from the campaign against IS. American combat troops left Iraq in 2011 but returned after the power vacuum led to the rise of IS in 2014.

The US could avoid repeating the same mistake by continuing to back the Peshmerga, said James Jeffrey, who spearheaded the global coalition against IS in Trump's first term.

"It's money well spent, as we found out when the Islamic State rolled into northern Iraq," said Jeffrey, a former US ambassador to Iraq and Turkey under the Obama administration.

The Trump administration has not said how many US troops brought in to fight IS more than a decade ago remain in Iraq. Experts believe it's under 1,000, down from 170,000 at the height of the Iraq War.

The recent meetings on Iraqi security included the White House, Defense and State Departments, with Tom Barrack acting as a principal US voice on Iraq, four sources said. A close Trump ally, Barrack is the US ambassador to Turkey and special envoy to Iraq and Syria.

The administration has said publicly it's open to a bilateral security agreement with Iraq. The countries discussed a possible defence pact in the recent meetings, but it's still unclear how the agreement might be structured or what Iraqi Kurdistan's role might be.

Al-Zaidi touted the troop withdrawal during his visit to Washington last month. Al-Zaidi, who was elected in May, met Trump at the White House, as well as Hegseth and members of Congress.

"October 1 will mark a new day in the trajectory of the Iraqi state, as Iraq will be free of any foreign military presence," al-Zaidi's office said in a statement at the time.

The withdrawal will reduce the exposure of US troops in the Middle East who have been targeted by Iran during the war, analysts said. Tehran has attacked US bases across the region, including the base in Irbil.

But it will leave the Peshmerga security force and the rest of the region it helps protect even more vulnerable than before, said Jason Campbell, a former US defence official.

"The Peshmerga have been the frontline in the US and international war with ISIS," said Campbell, an expert at the Middle East Institute. "If the US moves forward with this, it'll make the Kurds perhaps the most vulnerable potential targets of Iran."

articles.title: Las Vegas Valley converted 250 million sq ft of lawn to save water, saving 203 billion gallons; researchers found turf removal can raise summer land-surface temperatures about 20°C
articles.summary: US News: A major effort to remove grass lawns across the Las Vegas Valley has saved 203 billion gallons of water, but environmental research shows that the lar.
articles.body: A major effort to remove grass lawns across the Las Vegas Valley has saved 203 billion gallons of water, but environmental research shows that the large-scale change has also brought a serious rise in local surface temperatures. According to data from the Southern Nevada Water Authority’s Water Smart Landscapes Rebate programme, property owners across the metropolitan area have removed 250 million square feet of non-functional grass since 1999. The programme offers financial incentives of up to $5 per square foot to help residential and commercial property owners replace water-heavy lawns with desert landscaping and drip irrigation. The push gained legal backing after the Nevada Legislature passed Assembly Bill 356, alongside earlier laws including the Nevada Revised Statutes Water Conservation and Colorado River Act. The law requires decorative, non-functional grass to be removed from commercial properties, multi-family buildings, government sites and homeowners association properties across the region. However, scientific research into the effects of large-scale grass removal has found that getting rid of lawns can also raise local surface temperatures, particularly during the hottest months of summer.The heat caused by removing grassA study published in the academic journal Urban Climate found that removing turf grass in the Las Vegas Valley increased summer land-surface temperatures by 20 ± 0.3 Kelvin, or about 20°C. Researchers examined surface energy, sunlight reflection and evapotranspiration across urban, rural and barren parts of the dry valley. Grass lawns naturally cool their surroundings by releasing water through evapotranspiration. Replacing them with bare gravel, rocks, artificial grass or hard surfaces removes much of that cooling effect. "Turf grass removal increased temperatures by 20 ± 0.3 K, while urbanization, in general, increased LST by 5 ± 0.3 K," the researchers wrote in the Urban Climate study. They also noted that commercial buildings and asphalt roads remain the main sources of the wider urban heat island effect across the valley. The researchers found that grass keeps land surfaces cooler, but it requires large amounts of water to do so. This creates a difficult choice for Las Vegas between protecting its limited water supply and reducing heat in neighbourhoods.Balancing Colorado River water and heatSouthern Nevada gets about 90 per cent of its drinking water from Lake Mead, the Colorado River reservoir that has faced long periods of drought over the past two decades. Since outdoor irrigation causes most of the water that cannot be recovered to be lost in the Las Vegas Valley, local planners have focused heavily on removing grass to stay within federal water limits. Water used indoors in Las Vegas is collected, treated and returned to the water system, eventually making its way back towards Lake Mead. Outdoor water used on grass, however, largely evaporates and cannot be recovered. The Southern Nevada Water Authority estimates that replacing decorative grass with desert plants can reduce outdoor water use on targeted properties by up to 55 per cent. To deal with the higher temperatures linked to grass removal, regional water agencies and urban forestry experts recommend replacing lawns with water-efficient landscapes that still provide plenty of tree cover. Deep-rooted shade trees watered through targeted drip systems can create cooler areas and reduce the heat absorbed by nearby surfaces without using the huge amounts of water needed to maintain traditional lawns. Recent development rules promoted by the Southern Nevada Water Authority also prevent new grass from being installed in the front and back yards of single-family homes. At the same time, local authorities are encouraging urban forestry programmes to make sure that removing lawns does not make desert neighbourhoods even more vulnerable to extreme heat.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Milo Yiannopoulos arrested by ICE
articles.summary: The far-right commentator and self-described internet troll was arrested at the airport in New Orleans for staying in the country after his visa expired, according to DHS.
articles.body: Milo Yiannopoulos, a self-described libertarian and professional internet troll who became known for his controversial right-wing political views, is in ICE custody. A spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security told NBC News that ICE arrested Yiannopoulos, a United Kingdom national, on Thursday at the Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport in Kenner, Louisiana. The DHS spokesperson said Yiannopoulos legally entered the U.S. on May 14, 2019, through New York City, but then “chose to overstay his welcome in violation of our nation’s laws.” Yiannopoulos was taken into ICE custody Thursday after “failing to show up for his immigration hearing” on July 22, prompting an immigration judge to issue a final order of removal against him, according to the spokesperson. “He will remain in ICE custody pending removal,” the spokesperson added. TMZ first reported Yiannopoulos’ ICE arrest. Yiannopoulos has ties to Kanye West, known now as Ye, and previously served as the rapper’s chief of staff when Ye tried to run for president in 2020 and 2024. He also worked at Ye’s clothing brand Yeezy, but resigned from that job two years ago after the singer announced he was launching an adult entertainment studio under his Yeezy brand, TMZ reported. Ye is scheduled to perform in Louisiana Friday night at the New Orleans Caesars Superdome. It’s unclear whether Yiannopoulos was in the state to attend the concert. A former editor for Breitbart, the conservative internet publication President Donald Trump once considered one of his favorite news sources, Yiannopoulos resigned from the role in 2017 amid backlash to his reported comments about teens and sexual abuse. The DHS spokesperson said that the Trump administration is “working diligently to ensure that aliens in our country illegally can no longer fly unless it is out of our country to self-deport.”

articles.title: In 1983, scientists poured dye into Wyoming’s Popo Agie River before it vanished underground; two hours later, it resurfaced about 3,500 feet away with more water than entered
articles.summary: US News: In Sinks Canyon State Park in west-central Wyoming, the Middle Popo Agie River does something few rivers do: it disappears underground. At a point kno.
articles.body: In Sinks Canyon State Park in west-central Wyoming, the Middle Popo Agie River does something few rivers do: it disappears underground. At a point known as the Sinks, the river's entire flow vanishes into a cave system instead of continuing along an open channel. Downstream, the water reemerges at a separate location known as the Rise, where springs return the river to the surface. Although the underground relationship between the two points had long been recognised, U.S. Geological Survey hydrologists wanted to establish the connection through a direct test. In August 1983, they released fluorescent dye into the Middle Popo Agie at the Sinks and monitored water downstream at the Rise for the tracer's return. The dye appeared at the Rise about two hours later, providing direct evidence that water entering the Sinks travels through the underground system before resurfacing at the Rise. Researchers recovered about 84 per cent of the injected dye during the investigation, providing further evidence of the connection.How USGS hydrologists tested the underground connection at Sinks CanyonAccording to the U.S. Geological Survey's report on dye tracing in Wyoming, researchers used rhodamine WT, a fluorescent tracer commonly employed in hydrological investigations. The dye was released directly into the Middle Popo Agie at the Sinks, where the river disappears beneath the surface. Hydrologists then collected water samples at the Rise and analysed them for the dye's fluorescent signature. Dye tracing provides a way to establish underground connections that cannot be followed visually, allowing researchers to determine whether water introduced at one location subsequently appears at another. At Sinks Canyon, the experiment provided a direct test of whether the river disappearing at the Sinks was connected to the water emerging at the Rise.Why the dye appeared at the Rise just two hours laterThe fluorescent tracer reached the Rise approximately two hours after it was released at the Sinks. Researchers recovered about 84 per cent of the injected dye through their sampling, providing strong evidence of a hydraulic connection between the two locations. The speed of the tracer's movement was particularly notable because the river's path between the two points is largely hidden from view. Rather than relying only on the surrounding geology or the visible direction of the river, researchers could track the water through the underground system using a measurable chemical tracer. The experiment therefore established a measurable link between the Sinks and Rise and provided an estimate of how quickly water could travel through the underground system.What the experiment revealed about underground waterways in WyomingThe Sinks Canyon investigation was part of a broader series of dye-tracing studies conducted by the USGS to investigate groundwater movement and underground connections in Wyoming. Such tests are particularly useful in areas where soluble rock has created caves, underground channels and other pathways that allow water to move beneath the surface. Other Wyoming investigations produced very different results. In a 1970 test, dye released into the North Fork Powder River below Dullknife Reservoir took about 16 hours to travel 5.8 miles downstream to a spring. The journey included a stretch of about 0.6 miles where the river crossed a limestone outcrop and disappeared completely underground before resurfacing. A 1974 test on the Little Tongue River produced another result: only about 35 per cent of the injected dye was recovered at a cave roughly 2.6 miles away. The differing results demonstrate why dye tracing is useful for mapping underground water movement, since surface geography alone cannot always reveal where water travels once it disappears.Why the Sinks and Rise remain one of Wyoming's strangest river featuresAt the Sinks, the Middle Popo Agie appears to end abruptly as its flow disappears into the cave system. Just downstream, the Rise returns that water to the surface, creating a geological feature that looks almost impossible without knowing what lies beneath the canyon. The 1983 USGS experiment transformed that visible curiosity into a documented hydrological connection. By releasing a fluorescent tracer at the point where the river disappears and detecting it downstream only about two hours later, researchers were able to follow the river through a section of its journey that cannot be seen from the surface. The result is one of the clearest examples of how dye tracing can reveal hidden connections between surface rivers and underground waterways: at Sinks Canyon, the Middle Popo Agie does not simply disappear. Its water continues through the subsurface before emerging again at the Rise.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
